candidates.label: Metastatic melanoma to the liver from an occult primary
missing_or_uncertain: Primary site not identified; no skin lesion documented

candidates.label: Primary hepatic melanoma (extremely rare)
missing_or_uncertain: Extreme rarity; no extrahepatic primary found

candidates.label: Perivascular epithelioid cell tumor (PEComa) of the liver
missing_or_uncertain: SOX10 positivity is atypical for PEComa; BRAF V600E not typical

candidates.label: Clear cell sarcoma (melanocytic variant) metastatic to liver
missing_or_uncertain: BRAF V600E mutation is not typical; usually EWSR1 rearrangement

candidates.label: Malignant melanotic nerve sheath tumor (melanotic schwannoma) of the liver
missing_or_uncertain: BRAF V600E not typical; usually associated with Carney complex

response.rationale: The immunophenotype (HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, BRAF V600E) and melanin pigments strongly indicate a melanocytic neoplasm. Negative cytokeratin rules out carcinoma. The most common scenario is metastatic melanoma from an occult primary, given the absence of a known primary. Primary hepatic melanoma is extremely rare. Other melanocytic tumors like PEComa or clear cell sarcoma are less likely due to SOX10 positivity and BRAF V600E mutation.
